end.summary:
Used substitution to evaluate expressions such as c + 2.
Noted the pattern in 5n for different values of n.
Compared n + 3 and 3n using n = 1 and n = 2.
Read some expressions as situations, but teach-back was not passed.
Mixed up letters with object labels and questioned whether different letters can have the same number.
end.parentNote: Asha practised substituting values into expressions and comparing n + 3 with 3n; Laksh explained the 5n pattern and correctly solved c + 2 = 9 and c + 2 = 12. Laksh mixed up letters with object labels and remained unsure whether different letters may have the same number, so this was not corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, use short examples such as “n pencils cost ₹5 each” and ask what 5n means before choosing a value for n.
